account: In the early hours of Thursday 11 May 2023, a joint investigation by Focos Occidente and the Brigada de Investigación Criminal of Chile's Policía de Investigaciones led to 30 search warrants across Maipú, Pudahuel, Cerro Navia and other comunas. There were 17 detentions. Ten of them were linked to “encerronas” (robbery with intimidation or violence) whose perpetrators posted their robberies on TikTok. On 12 May 2023 the television channel T13 quoted Fiscal Nacional Ángel Valencia saying that the algorithm accelerates criminal analysis. T13 reports that after three members were arrested, the model searched their links and raised persons of interest whom victims later identified. The Fiscalía de Chile's regional news release of 17 May 2023 says that the ten were identified through the software Fiscal Heredia (Herramienta para el Estudio del Delito Usando Inteligencia Artificial). The release describes it as an AI model developed by several universities and incorporated into the Ministerio Público in March 2023. The model proposes probable participants from prosecution and police records for prosecutors and police to work up. The Noveno Juzgado de Garantía accredited the eight robberies. Four adults went to preventive detention, and four adolescents remained in provisional internment. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the case. On 25 August 2026 the Fiscalía named the developers as the Universidad de Chile, the Universidad del Biobío and the Universidad de los Andes. They worked with the Ministerio Público in a project, funded by the Fondo de Fomento al Desarrollo Científico y Tecnológico (Fondef), that began in 2020. The Fiscalía reported that the tool, now called Fiscal HeredIA, runs in 15 regional prosecutor's offices with more than 1,000 prosecutors and other users. It also reported that the tool won second place in the IFORS Prize for OR in Development 2026.

ai_role.statement: The deploying public body credits the AI with the identification of probable participants, complemented by prosecutors' and police work and victim identification. T13 adds the mechanism (link search from three arrested members). No court document or independent evaluation of the model's accuracy is among the sources. The Fiscalía is both the source and the beneficiary.

display.answer: After initial arrests, investigators searched links to those suspects, reviewed people whom Fiscal Heredia proposed, and sought victim identification before further action.

value.text: After initial arrests, investigators searched links to those suspects, reviewed people whom Fiscal Heredia proposed, and sought victim identification before further action.

purpose: Build networks of links among people with criminal records to propose probable members of a group tied to a specific crime. This reduces the case files prosecutors must review.

ratings.reason: The prosecutor's office reported that a gang responsible for at least eight accredited violent robberies was detained and brought before the Noveno Juzgado de Garantía. Four adults went to preventive detention.
Prosecutors state that the tool replaces review of hundreds of case files with a short list of proposed links.

must_hold: Suspects must already appear in the records the model draws on
Legal basis for cross-agency data linkage
produced_by: Linked prosecution, prison and police records (SAF, Gendarmería, Carabineros)
A few confirmed arrests seeding a link search
Victim identification to confirm proposed persons of interest
